title: VSWR and Return Loss
summary: reflection coefficient, standing-wave ratio, and return loss for impedance matching.
body:
when a transmission line is not matched to its load, part of the wave reflects.
the reflection coefficient gamma quantifies this; VSWR and return loss are two
ways of expressing the same mismatch. a perfect match is gamma = 0, VSWR = 1:1,
and infinite return loss.
examples: 75 ohm load on a 50 ohm line: gamma = (75-50)/(75+50) = 0.2, VSWR = 1.5:1, RL = 14 dB.
VSWR 2:1 reflects ~11% of power -- usually the acceptable upper limit for antennas.
gotchas: return loss is sometimes quoted negative; the magnitude is what matters (higher = better match)
VSWR ignores cable loss, which actually improves the VSWR measured at the input (masking a bad antenna)
a Smith chart plots gamma on the complex plane; these scalar formulas assume purely resistive loads
